description: Jailbreak attack classes and the candidate models used to evaluate safety behavior in the Jailbreak Playground.

attack_categories.name: Role Manipulation
attack_categories.description: Attempt to change the AI's identity or rules.
attack_categories.learning_objective: Recognize that a model's identity is fixed and role changes are forced input.

attack_categories.name: Context Switching
attack_categories.description: Use multiple messages to frame a shifting context that slides past a refusal.
attack_categories.learning_objective: Evaluate the model across the full conversation, not a single prompt.

attack_categories.name: Instruction Conflict
attack_categories.description: Provide conflicting or higher-priority directives to confuse the model.
attack_categories.learning_objective: Separate authoritative instructions from untrusted embedded data.

attack_categories.name: Encoding Attempts
attack_categories.description: Use unusual formatting, Base64, leetspeak or crafted wordplay to hide intent.
attack_categories.learning_objective: See that obfuscation does not change the resolved safety verdict.

attack_categories.name: Multi-turn Attacks
attack_categories.description: Chain several messages to gradually relax the model's guardrails.
attack_categories.learning_objective: Study persistent, stateful attacks that span the full history.

attack_categories.name: Social Engineering
attack_categories.description: Apply authority, urgency, flattery, or empathy to make the model share or leak.
attack_categories.learning_objective: Know that psychological pressure on the model is untrusted data, not proof.

models.name: Sentinel-Lite
models.description: An early, permissive model with shallow alignment. It passes simple cases but fails under framing, encoding and pressure.

models.name: Sentinel-Pro
models.description: A hardened model with stronger alignment and layered guardrails. It holds the line across most nuanced adversarial tests.
